offence_severity: Life imprisonment / Rigorous imprisonment for varying terms
physical_harm: Injuries caused to P.W. 7 and 8, including head and hand injuries, and the deceased suffered head injuries
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the ocular evidence of the injured witnesses P.W. 7 and 8, their statements recorded at the hospital, and the testimony of P.W. 11, the officer-in-charge of the police station.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the injured witnesses P.W. 7 and 8 based on their oral evidence, their statements recorded at the hospital, and the testimony of P.W. 11, noting that the absence of injury reports was a defective investigation but did not discredit their credibility as injured witnesses.
post_offence_conduct: The appellants were directed to surrender forthwith to serve out the remaining period of their sentence.
trial_duration: The occurrence is said to have taken place on 01.11.1983. The trial judgment was delivered on 28.05.2009 by the High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi. The Supreme Court decision was delivered on 04.10.2019.
legal_representation: For the Appellant: Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Adv., Sudarshan Rajan, Dr. K. B. Sounder Rajan, Mahesh Kumar, Vijay Kumar Sharma, Ms. Mehaak Jaggi, Ms. Ankita Tiwari, P. Narasimhan, Advs. For the Respondents: Anil K. Jha, Jayesh Gaurav, Ms. Diksha Ojha, Ms. Priyanka Tyagi, Kuldeep Rai, T. Mahipal, Advs.
investigation_status: The police report was lodged by P.W. 8 at the hospital. The officer-in-charge of the police station where the deceased and injured were taken, specifically deposed that he submitted a request for the injury report of the witnesses and pursuant to which their injury reports were made available to him. Only thereafter the charge sheet was submitted by him.
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under Sections 302/149, 323/149 and 147 IPC. High Court: Judgment and Order dated 28.05.2009. Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeals on 04.10.2019.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the charge under Section 147 was defective because it was framed against only four persons and not all six accused, without the aid of Sections 141 and 146. They also claimed that the evidence of the injured witnesses P.W. 7 and 8 was credible despite the absence of injury reports, and that the appellants were part of an unlawful assembly with a common object of murdering the deceased.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the charge under Section 147 was defective and that the appellants were seriously prejudiced in their defence because the questions put to them under Section 313 were inadequate and perfunctory, denying them the opportunity to present their defence. They also claimed that the absence of injury reports for P.W. 7 and 8 cast doubt on the credibility of the prosecution's case.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle of audi alteram partem under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, which provides the accused with an opportunity to explain circumstances appearing against them in the evidence. The court also emphasized that the absence of prejudice must be demonstrated for any challenge to the trial process.
precedent_relied_upon: Suresh Chandra Bahri v. State of Bihar 1995 Suppl (1) SCC 80; Shobhit Chamar v. State of Bihar, (1998) 3 SCC 455; Fahim Khan v. State of Bihar (2011) 13 SCC 142; Sukha v. State of Rajasthan [1956] SCR 288; Masalti v. State of U.P., AIR 1965 SC 202; Ranvir Yadav v. State of Bihar, (2009) 6 SCC 595; Samsul Haque v. State of Assam, (2019) (11) SCALE 458; Najabhai Desurbhai Wagh v. Valerabhai Deganbhai Vagh and Ors., (2017) 3 SCC 261
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the appellants were found to be members of an unlawful assembly that assaulted the deceased, with some of them armed with spears. The court found that the prosecution's case was supported by ocular evidence and that the appellants had not demonstrated any prejudice caused by the trial process.
other_sentence_order: The appeals were dismissed, and the appellants were directed to surrender forthwith to serve out the remaining period of their sentence. Their bail bonds were cancelled.
